The Peace of God
PEACE
noun phrase
From the Greek eirene, “peace” (answering to the Hebrew shalom, “wholeness, well-being”), the settled tranquillity of soul which God gives through Christ.

📖 Biblical Definition

The peace of God is that holy calm and settled rest of soul which God bestows upon His people through Christ, keeping their hearts amid every care and fear. Paul bids the saints be careful for nothing, but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving to let their requests be made known unto God; and then comes the promise: And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus (Phil 4:7). The dictionary marks this peace as a gift, not an achievement, and as a guardian, not a feeling only; for the word rendered “keep” is a soldier’s word, that the peace of God shall garrison the heart as a watch about a city. It passeth all understanding, for it is not the peace the world gives, which is bottomed on outward ease, but a peace that abides in tribulation, in want, in the prison, and at the stake. So the Scripture teaches that this peace flows from peace with God, made by the blood of the cross; for being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ (Rom 5:1). The Lord Himself bequeathed it: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you (Joh 14:27). It is therefore Christ’s own peace, lodged in the believer by His Spirit, ruling the heart and stilling the storm of care.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The settled tranquillity of soul which God gives through Christ, garrisoning the heart against all care and fear.

THE PEACE OF GOD, the settled calm of soul which God bestows through Christ.

📖 Key Scripture

Phil 4:7 — "And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus."

Joh 14:27 — "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid."

Rom 5:1 — "Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ:"

Isa 26:3 — "Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A treasure of Scripture; the settled rest of soul God gives through Christ, flowing from peace made by His blood.

expand to see more

The peace of God has drawn little redefinition from the present age, surviving as a comfort named in many a believer’s prayer. The dictionary records it that the reader may mark its true ground in peace with God, made by the blood of the cross, and not in mere outward ease.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the peace of God is a gift of grace, garrisoning the heart, and not a mood the soul works up in itself. It passeth all understanding because it abides where the world’s peace fails, in want and tribulation and at the stake; for it flows from peace with God through justification by faith in Christ. The world offers a peace bottomed on circumstance; Christ gives His own peace, lodged in the heart by His Spirit. Let the anxious soul cast its care upon God in prayer with thanksgiving, and the peace of God shall keep the heart and mind through Christ Jesus.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Greek eirene, answering the Hebrew shalom, the phrase names the soul’s rest given by God in Christ.
